# Drawer + Tabs (SFCC-195, SFCC-736) — plan

_Built incrementally with Tim, walking real Figma frames and Jira tickets, in `feature/sfcc-52-global-header`'s session on 2026-08-26/27. Saved here per the SFCC-52 precedent (`.docs/temp/SFCC-52-global-header-plan.md`) for review before any component code is written._

## Context

Building a reusable slide-out Drawer (right-anchored) and a reusable Tabs component for
Zimmermann PWA. Immediate scope is two stories:

- **SFCC-736 "pdp/drawer"** (assigned to Tim, Squad-A, In Progress) — the drawer _shell_ only:
  slide-in panel, backdrop overlay, close button, tab navigation header. Accepts tab content as
  children. Does not own tab content.
- **SFCC-195 "PDP – Slide Out - Details & Care"** — first tab's content (Details & Care),
  triggered by info links on PDP. Depends on SFCC-736's shell/tab API.

Known future consumers of the same Drawer/Tabs primitives (NOT in scope now, but the API must
stay generic enough for them): SFCC-102 (Size & Fit tab), SFCC-266 (EU Environmental Qualities
tab), SFCC-267 (Shipping & Returns + Assistance tabs), SFCC-101 (Measmerize/Find My Size CTA),
SFCC-742 (Wishlist login panel — renders as children inside pdp/drawer), SFCC-801 (global
country/currency selector — separate right-anchored drawer, same shape), **SFCC-297 (Find in
Boutique — confirmed by Tim to use this same Drawer)**. A story also exists for the Add to Cart /
View Cart mini-cart (not yet shared/ticketed here) — confirmed by Tim it will invoke this Drawer
to display the mini-cart once picked up, consistent with `cart.md` PRD's "opens as an overlay on
Add to Bag CTA or bag icon click."

## Research findings

- **No existing Tabs component anywhere** — not in `overrides/`, not in the base
  `@salesforce/retail-react-app` template (confirmed via full grep, zero `Tabs`/`TabList` usage
  and no theme recipe). Genuinely greenfield, no in-repo prior art.
- **`ZimmModal` + `useZimmModal`** (`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmModal/`,
  `overrides/app/hooks/useZimmModal.ts`) exist today but are fully hand-rolled — NOT built on
  Chakra's `Modal`/`Drawer` primitives. Centered/fixed-width only, no `placement` concept. Single
  consumer: `ZimmSubscribeModal` (newsletter capture, footer). Not Tier 2 yet (only 1 consumer).
  **Decision (updated): refactor in place onto Chakra's `Modal` primitive** — see Decisions made.
- **Add to Cart is NOT greenfield at the data layer.** `useShopperBasketsMutationHelper().
addItemToNewOrExistingBasket(productItems)` (from `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`) + existing
  `useCurrentBasket()` (inherited unmodified, Tier 1) already handle the full add-to-basket flow.
  A fully-wired confirmation UI already exists too: `AddToCartModal` +
  `AddToCartModalProvider`/`useAddToCartModalContext()` (base
  `app/hooks/use-add-to-cart-modal.js`), mounted at app root, built on Chakra `Modal` (not
  Drawer). No mini-cart/cart-drawer exists in the base app yet. **Tim confirmed a story already
  exists** for this (not yet shared) — when picked up, it will invoke our new Drawer to display
  the mini-cart. The correct approach is shadowing `use-add-to-cart-modal.js` and swapping its
  Modal primitives for our Drawer, reusing the existing context/hook plumbing and data layer
  as-is — not building new cart data logic.
- **`protectedFiles.md`'s Tier 2 "Shared Hooks" list is NOT aspirational** (correcting an earlier
  wrong read) — all 8 named hooks (`use-auth-modal`, `use-toast`, `use-modal-state`,
  `use-intersection-observer`, `use-currency`, `use-dnt-notification`, `use-app-origin`,
  `use-selected-store`) exist fully-built in the base template today, several genuinely
  5+-consumer, none stubs. They just aren't overridden in `overrides/` yet. Tier 2 protection
  applies the moment one is overridden.
  - **`use-modal-state.js`** (base): `useModalState({closeOnRouteChange, resetDataOnClose}) =>
{isOpen, data, onOpen(data), onClose()}`, auto-closes on route change. Currently 3 consumers
    in base (bonus-product-selection-modal subsystem).
  - **`use-auth-modal.js`** (base): `AuthModal` component + `useAuthModal(initialView)` — full
    login/register/reset/passwordless modal system, already reused 3x (`_app`,
    `with-registration` gate wrapper, checkout contact-info). Directly relevant to SFCC-742
    (wishlist login panel) — the `with-registration` wrapper is a reusable gate-the-action
    pattern, not something to build fresh.
- **Base `drawer-menu`** (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/drawer-menu/
drawer-menu.jsx`, inherited unmodified in this repo) is a real, working Chakra `Drawer`
  implementation: `Drawer`/`DrawerOverlay`/`DrawerContent`/`DrawerHeader`/`DrawerBody`/
  `DrawerFooter`/`DrawerCloseButton`, `placement="left"`, responsive `size` via
  `useBreakpointValue`, multi-part theme styling via `useMultiStyleConfig('DrawerMenu')`
  (project theme file `theme/components/project/drawer-menu.js`), focus-trap/scroll-lock
  inherited for free from Chakra (not hand-rolled). This is the reference pattern for the new
  drawer.
- **PRD vocabulary is deliberate**: `pdp.md` distinguishes "slide-out/flyout" from "modal" in 3
  places (Find in Boutique, Size Guide). `checkout.md` contradicted this once (calls Find in
  Boutique a "modal") — **fixed**: `checkout.md`'s CFD-043 line now says "Find in Boutique
  drawer," consistent with `pdp.md` and with Find in Boutique (SFCC-297) confirmed as a Drawer
  consumer. `homepage.md`'s "Join Us" capture (already built as `ZimmSubscribeModal`) is a
  genuine confirmed centered Modal — so both patterns are real and intentionally distinct in
  this codebase.

## Decisions made

1. **New Drawer built on Chakra's native `Drawer` primitive**, following the `drawer-menu`
   precedent — inherits focus-trap/scroll-lock/ESC handling from Chakra for free. Styled
   entirely via a new Zimmermann project theme recipe (co-located `.css.ts` per
   `overrideStyling.md`'s pattern), not inline props.
2. **The "generic hook for other developers" is an override of base's `use-modal-state.js`**
   (`overrides/app/hooks/use-modal-state.ts`), not a new custom hook — this becomes Tier 2
   protected the moment it's created, per `protectedFiles.md`.
3. **One Modal system, not two — `ZimmModal`/`useZimmModal` refactored in place onto Chakra's
   `Modal` primitive** (updated from an earlier "leave it untouched, two architectures coexist"
   draft — Tim doesn't want two different dialog implementations in the codebase). Same
   component name, same public props (`isOpen`, `mounted`, `onClose`, `maxWidth`, `labelledBy`,
   `describedBy`, `children`) and same hook name/shape as far as the one existing consumer
   (`ZimmSubscribeModal`) needs — only the internals swap from the hand-rolled
   portal/focus-trap/scroll-lock to Chakra's `Modal`/`ModalOverlay`/`ModalContent`. Verify
   `ZimmSubscribeModal`'s existing story/tests still pass unchanged after the refactor — that's
   the acceptance bar, not a rewrite of its own code. In scope for the
   `feature/sfcc-736-pdp-drawer-tabs` worktree (foundational dialog work, not tied to PDP), done
   alongside/before building the new `Drawer`.
4. **SFCC-195 scope is component-only for this pass.** Its AC requires "click a PDP info link →
   drawer opens," but `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/` doesn't exist yet at all (fully
   inherited from base SFCC) — wiring a real trigger means copy-first-ing a large base file tree
   (`product-detail/index.jsx`, `product-view/index.jsx`, dependents), a separate, much larger
   initiative. **Decision: build the Details & Care tab content component + Storybook
   demonstration of open/close only. Do not touch the PDP page in this pass** — real PDP wiring
   is deferred/flagged as follow-up work, not silently dropped.

## Figma walkthrough — findings

### Drawer Page / Large (node `40002218:42893`, `pdp/drawer/large`)

- Frame 1440×1024. `Background Overlay` is a full-canvas backdrop rect (1440×1024) — the
  perceived "grey only on the left" is the drawer panel instance sitting on top of it, not the
  overlay itself being partial-width.
- Drawer panel instance (`pdp/drawer`, x=720, width=720) = **exactly 720/1440 = 50%**, confirming
  **Large = 50% of screen** precisely.
- Panel instance splits into `pdp/drawer/header` (720×120) and `pdp/drawer/content` (720×750).

### Header structure (`pdp/drawer/header` → `drawer/header`, 592×24, inset 64px/48px inside the

120px-tall header container)

- **`Menu`** — row of `drawer/nav-item` instances: Details & Care, Size Guide, Find My Size,
  Shipping & Returns, Assistance (visible) + a **6th nav-item present but `hidden`** — almost
  certainly the EU Environmental Qualities tab (SFCC-266), confirming the design already treats
  it as a conditional 6th slot, matching its AC ("must only render when `environmentalNotes` is
  populated, no empty state"). Item gap = 24px.
  - Also 2 `Overflow`-named elements in the same Menu frame, both `hidden` — **no real overflow
    visual exists in Figma yet** (confirmed with user). Behavior instead confirmed verbally:
    **chevrons render only when the next nav item doesn't fit in the available header width**
    (a width-measurement/overflow-detection problem, not a fixed tab-count threshold — matters
    because tab labels come from Contentful and vary in length). No design reference for the
    interaction once shown (scroll-one-at-a-time vs. partial-reveal-to-hint, etc.) — open item.
- **`Navigation icon group`** (separate from Menu, trailing) — `Chevron group` (left+right
  chevron, 4px apart) then `Close`. Confirms chevrons + close are a fixed trailing slot, chevron
  visibility conditional per above, close always visible.
- **Naming note**: Figma tab label reads "SIZE GUIDE" where Jira AC says "Size & Fit" — user
  confirmed this is fine since **all tab labels/content come from Contentful** and are editable;
  content model design needed (see Open Items) rather than hardcoded label constants.

### zimm-\* token mapping for observed measurements (source: `zimmTokens.ts` + `spacing.ts` +

`sizes.ts`)

| Figma measurement                     | Token                                                                      |
| ------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Header 64px horizontal inset          | `var(--zimm-scale-4xl)` (spacing.4xl = 4rem = 64px)                        |
| Header 48px vertical inset            | `var(--zimm-scale-1200)` (numeric alias, 48px — no named-scale equivalent) |
| 24px gap between nav items            | `var(--zimm-scale-xl)` (spacing.xl = 1.5rem = 24px)                        |
| 16px chevron/close icon size          | `var(--zimm-icon-size-md)` (iconSizes.md = 16px)                           |
| 4px gap between the two chevron icons | `var(--zimm-scale-2xs)` (spacing['2xs'] = 0.25rem = 4px)                   |

**Reminder for implementation**: per `overrideStyling.md`/`css.md`, always reference these as
`var(--zimm-*)` CSS custom properties in component code — never the bare Chakra/theme token key
(`spacing.xl`, `'xl'`), even though both resolve to the same value.

### Drawer Page / Small (node `40002218:42900`, `pdp/drawer/small`)

- Panel instance x=1038, width=402 → **402/1440 = 27.9%**, not exactly 25% — flagged, not yet
  explained (possible min-readable-width floor; not confirmed). **Resolved**: implement Small's
  width as an actual `25%` behind a named variable/token (not the observed 27.9%, not a raw
  literal) — Tim will flag the Figma discrepancy to the design team separately.
- **Two different content examples exist at Small** — a single-purpose "NOTIFY" (back-in-stock)
  form with a plain title header (no tabs, just `NOTIFY` + close `X`), and a separate "Details &
  Care" tabbed example (symbol `Size=Small`, node `40002218:43001`, 402×1024) — confirms the
  Drawer header supports at least two variants: **simple title** vs. **tabbed nav**, reused by
  different consumers at the same width.
- **This resolves the open Jira question about tab-header behavior at Small 25%.** Header
  container 402×104 (vs Large's 720×120), inner row inset **32px horizontal / 40px vertical**
  (vs Large's 64px/48px) — `var(--zimm-scale-2xl)` (32px) / `var(--zimm-scale-3xl)` (40px), both
  clean named-scale matches. `Menu` content area = 254px. Screenshot confirms only **`DETAILS &
CARE` + `SIZE GUIDE`** fit before chevrons activate — direct visual confirmation of the
  width-based overflow trigger rule. Trailing `Navigation icon group` (76px: `Chevron group` +
  `Close`) unchanged in internal structure from Large, just repositioned narrower.
- Note: Figma's raw node widths for individual `drawer/nav-item` instances (30px boxes) don't
  reflect real text-rendered width at either size — a metadata tool quirk, not a real 30px tab
  width. Treat the screenshot as ground truth for actual visible-tab-count; metadata for
  structure/grouping/hidden-slot presence only.

### Drawer Page / Mobile (node `40002218:42903`, `pdp/drawer/mobile`)

- Frame 402×956, drawer panel instance 402×878 — **full width** (matches AC 9 "full-width from
  left to right"), but **78px of backdrop still visible below the panel** (956-878=78), i.e. does
  NOT reach the bottom of the screen — confirms AC 9's "leaves a small piece of background open
  at the bottom" exactly. 78px is close to but not an exact match for `var(--zimm-scale-5xl)`
  (80px) — flag as approximate pending exact redline/dev-mode confirmation, don't hardcode 78px
  as if it were precise.
  - **Resolved**: Tim's initial read was that this gap might just be unfilled example content
    rather than a deliberate spec, and asked whether to build full-height instead. But AC 9 is
    PO-approved with an explained rationale (Dani Rivett, 2026-08-21: "the team's preference was
    that some of the background still showed so a user can easily navigate out") — a deliberate,
    documented UX decision, not an accident. **Decision: keep the gap as built (near-full height,
    not 100vh), and separately flag to design/PO to reconfirm AC 9 still stands** rather than
    silently dropping an approved, explained requirement. Don't hardcode the exact 78px — use a
    token-backed value and let design confirm the precise number.
- Tab header shows the **same 2-tabs-then-chevron pattern as Small** (`DETAILS & CARE` +
  `SIZE GUIDE` visible, rest behind chevrons) — since Mobile and Small share the same 402px
  content width, this is good evidence the overflow trigger is genuinely a pure
  width-measurement check, not a breakpoint-name special case (i.e. don't hardcode "show N tabs
  on mobile" — measure available width against real rendered tab widths).

### Details & Care content structure (node `40001889:38504`, `Size=Large, Tab=Details & Care,

Variant=Default`) — SFCC-195's actual scope

- Three repeating `{Sub-header, Body}` blocks: **Product Description** (title + description
  bullets), **Material**, **Care** — plus a trailing **Style Code** line under Care. All
  confirmed by user as SFCC-sourced (not Contentful).
- Consistent spacing rhythm, clean token matches: **64px between every section**
  (`var(--zimm-scale-4xl)`) and **20px between each sub-header and its body**
  (`var(--zimm-scale-l)`).
- **Resolved (partially)**: AC 4 only names three merge fields (`{{display-name}}`,
  `{{long-description}}`, `{{careInstructions}}`) but the design has 4 content blocks + Style
  Code. User decided: **treat `Material` as its own distinct SFCC product attribute** (not a
  parsed/split piece of `long-description`) — component prop shape should have a dedicated
  `material` field alongside `displayName`/`longDescription`/`careInstructions`. **Still open**:
  exact SFCC attribute ID for `material` (and for Style Code — likely a SKU/style-number field,
  still unconfirmed) needs verification in Business Manager — Tim will check and confirm.
  Don't hardcode an attribute ID until confirmed.

## Component architecture (3 layers)

1. **`ZimmDrawer`** (new, generic, atom-tier — `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmDrawer/`,
   as implemented — this section originally planned it unprefixed at `atoms/drawer/`, before the
   `Zimm`-prefix naming convention was applied consistently to new ui-kits components) — fully
   generic right-anchored slide-in shell. Chakra-native (`Drawer`/`DrawerOverlay`/
   `DrawerContent`/`DrawerCloseButton`), `placement="right"`. Header content is a plain slot
   (children) — ZimmDrawer itself knows nothing about tabs, so SFCC-801/742's simple-title-header
   use case and SFCC-736's tabbed use case both compose on top of it. Styled via a co-located
   `zimmDrawer.css.ts` recipe (custom widths for Large/Small — Chakra's default `size` scale
   doesn't have 50%/25% steps).
   - `size: 'large' | 'small' | 'mobile'` prop (matches SFCC-742's own `Large | Small | Mobile`
     convention). Small's width is a named token/variable set to `25%` (not the 27.9% observed
     in the current Figma frame — flagged to design separately, don't build to the observed
     number). **X-Large excluded from the type for now** — design is still WIP, add when ready
     rather than building against an unfinished spec.
   - **Resolved**: `size="large"`/`size="small"` collapse to the Mobile treatment automatically
     below the mobile breakpoint (media-query override, per `overrideStyling.md`'s "explicit
     media queries" pattern) — confirmed by Tim: resizing the browser to mobile width should
     always yield the mobile drawer regardless of the chosen `size`. `mobile` as an explicit
     value is still needed for SFCC-742's convention, but the responsive collapse happens
     automatically too.
2. **`ZimmTabs`** (new, generic, molecule-tier — `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmTabs/`,
   as implemented — same `Zimm`-prefix naming note as above; originally planned unprefixed at
   `molecules/tabs/`) — standalone tab switcher, usable anywhere (not drawer-specific). Owns the
   width-measurement overflow logic: chevrons appear only when the next tab doesn't fit
   (`ResizeObserver`-based measurement). **Chevron click behavior confirmed: scroll by one tab
   per click** (not reveal-all-remaining, not multi-tab pagination) — resolves the earlier open
   question. Needs real logic so gets its own `index.test.tsx`, not just a story.
3. **`ZimmPdpDrawer`** (new, organism-tier — `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmPdpDrawer/`,
   as implemented — same naming note; originally planned unprefixed at `organisms/pdpDrawer/`) —
   the actual SFCC-736 deliverable, matching the Figma `pdp/drawer` component and its AC exactly:
   composes `ZimmDrawer` + `ZimmTabs` internally, exposes a simple `tabs: {id, label,
content}[]` prop so PDP-specific stories (SFCC-102/266/267/101, SFCC-195) don't need to know
   about the ZimmDrawer/ZimmTabs composition at all.
4. **`ZimmModal`/`useZimmModal` refactor** (existing component, not new) — internals rebuilt on
   Chakra's `Modal` primitive per Decision 3 above. Same public API, `ZimmSubscribeModal` (the
   one existing consumer) should need no code changes — verify its story/tests still pass after
   the refactor.

**The "generic hook for other developers" ask is `overrides/app/hooks/use-modal-state.ts`** —
copy-first override of base's `use-modal-state.js` (`{closeOnRouteChange, resetDataOnClose} =>
{isOpen, data, onOpen(data), onClose()}`), becomes Tier 2 protected per `protectedFiles.md` the
moment it's created. This is what any future consumer (SFCC-742, 801, a future cart drawer) uses
to manage open/close state before handing `isOpen`/`onClose` to `ZimmDrawer`.

**Comments discipline**: per `conventions.md`, default to no comments in new code — only add one
where the *why* is genuinely non-obvious (e.g. the 25%-vs-27.9% Figma discrepancy, or the AC
9/PO-rationale for the mobile gap). Keep any that are needed short and to the point.

## Worktree / dependency structure

Two worktrees, both branched off `develop` (second one dependent on the first), following the
`.claude/worktrees/feature+<slug>` convention established by the SFCC-52 initiative:

1. **`.claude/worktrees/feature+sfcc-736-pdp-drawer-tabs`**
   (`feature/sfcc-736-pdp-drawer-tabs`, off `origin/develop`) — builds `ZimmDrawer`, `ZimmTabs`,
   `ZimmPdpDrawer`, and the `use-modal-state.ts` override. This is the foundational, unblocked
   worktree — start here. **This plan doc lives here.**
2. **`.claude/worktrees/feature+sfcc-195-details-care`**
   (`feature/sfcc-195-details-care`, branched from `feature/sfcc-736-pdp-drawer-tabs`, not
   `develop`) — builds the Details & Care tab content component (presentational, receives
   product data as props per `components.md`'s container/presentational rule: `displayName`,
   `longDescription`, `material`, `careInstructions`, `styleCode` — exact SFCC attribute IDs for
   `material`/`styleCode` still pending Business Manager check) + a Storybook story
   demonstrating it inside `PdpDrawer`. Rebase onto `develop` once SFCC-736 merges.

Both worktrees already created as of this doc being written. Tier touch check (Hard Rule 10):
both worktrees stay within Tier 4 (new components) + one Tier 2 touch each (SFCC-736 registers
new recipes in `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts`, UI Designer notify per
`protectedFiles.md`; SFCC-195 touches nothing Tier 1/2 at all since PDP wiring is deferred). No
multi-tier violation.

## Open items / not yet resolved

- Original Jira links on SFCC-736 (node `2400-36912`) and SFCC-195 (none attached) were wrong/
  missing — correct node links now captured per breakpoint above (Large `40002218:42893`, Small
  `40002218:42900`/`40002218:43001`, Mobile `40002218:42903`, Details & Care content
  `40001889:38504`). **Follow-up: update the Jira tickets with these corrected links.**
- **Two items to flag to the design team** (Tim will do this): (1) Small's measured width in
  Figma is 27.9%, not the named 25% — we're building to 25% via a token regardless; (2) Mobile's
  ~78px bottom gap (AC 9) — reconfirm the requirement still stands given the example content may
  not have filled the viewport, even though we're keeping the gap as built pending that
  confirmation.
- **Tab CONTENT model is mixed-source, not uniformly Contentful** — Tim clarified Details & Care
  (SFCC-195) is actually **product data** (SFCC attributes `display-name`, `long-description`,
  `careInstructions`, per its AC), not CMS content, and confirmed this bucket is **SFCC-only, no
  Contentful blending**. Cross-referencing the other tab tickets shows three distinct sourcing
  patterns across the same Drawer shell:
  1. **Product/commerce-attribute driven, SFCC only**: Details & Care (SFCC-195); EU
     Environmental Qualities (SFCC-266, sourced from the `environmentalNotes` product attribute
     via MuleSoft/AP21 — data pipeline, not Contentful authoring).
  2. **Contentful-managed**: Shipping & Returns + Assistance (SFCC-267, explicitly
     "content-managed in Contentful, no code deployment to update"); Size Guide (SFCC-102,
     "managed in Contentful per product type").
  3. **Third-party widget embed**: Find My Size / Measmerize (SFCC-101) — not our content at all.
  - **Implication for the content model**: only tab _labels_ are uniformly Contentful-drivable —
    per-tab body content needs a discriminated-union-shaped contract, not one generic "Drawer
    Tab" Contentful type for everything. Any Contentful modeling here should still be a generic
    referenceable primitive for the tabs that genuinely are CMS content (bucket 2) — but bucket 1
    tabs should NOT be forced into that same Contentful shape. Confirms SFCC-195's tab content
    component should be a presentational component receiving product data as props, not a
    Contentful-fetching component. Content model design for bucket 2 still needs its own pass —
    not yet scoped.
- **"Each tab expands inline" (SFCC-195 description) does NOT mean an accordion** — confirmed via
  the Size & Fit reference frame (`Size=Large, Tab=Size & Fit, Variant=Default`, SFCC-102, shown
  for reference only): it's a single tall vertical scroll (description → tables → CM/INCH toggle),
  no collapse/expand sections. "Expands inline" just means content appears within the drawer on
  tab switch. Also reinforces AC 10 (tab content scrolls independently of the header) — this
  reference content (1283px) is well taller than the drawer's content viewport.
- Exact SFCC attribute IDs for `material` and Style Code (Details & Care content) — pending
  Business Manager check.
- Contentful content model for the genuinely CMS-driven tabs (Shipping & Returns, Assistance,
  Size Guide) needs its own design pass — not yet scoped.
- Real PDP wiring (info link → drawer open) deferred out of SFCC-195's scope — needs a decision
  on when/how the PDP page itself gets its first override.
- Add to Cart / View Cart mini-cart story (confirmed to exist) not yet shared with this session —

## ZimmTabs keyboard accessibility fix (2026-08-31)

Tim reported: pressing Tab inside an open drawer moves between the active tab and the close
icon instead of cycling the other tab headers, and asked for Tab-to-move/Enter-to-activate
behaviour. Checked this against the actual spec before changing anything (WCAG 2.1 SC 2.1.1 +
WAI-ARIA APG's Tabs pattern, both fetched live) rather than assuming either the bug report or a
"just make it accessible" reflex fix was right:

- **WCAG 2.1.1 doesn't mandate Tab-based navigation for a composite widget** — any keyboard
  path satisfies it.
- **WAI-ARIA's Tabs pattern is explicit**: `Tab` moves focus into/out of the tablist as a whole
  (arrives on the active tab, leaves to the next focusable element outside it — the close icon,
  here); Left/Right/Home/End move *within* the tablist. Two activation models exist —
  **automatic** (arrow keys switch the panel immediately, no Enter needed) is recommended
  specifically "when panel content is not costly to display," which is exactly this case
  (static content, no fetch). **Manual** (Enter/Space required) is for the opposite case.
- `ZimmTabs` already implemented automatic activation with Left/Right and a roving tabIndex —
  the reported "bug" was actually the Tab key behaving per spec. Confirmed with Tim to keep
  automatic activation and fix the real, separate gap instead: no `aria-controls`/`id` linking
  each tab to its panel, so a screen reader couldn't announce what a tab controls.

**Fixed:**
- `ZimmTabs`: added `Home`/`End` key support (jump to first/last tab); new required `ariaLabel`
  prop (the tablist itself needs an accessible name — no visible on-page label exists for it,
  per APG) and `idPrefix` prop, each tab now gets `id={idPrefix}-tab-{tab.id}` and
  `aria-controls={idPrefix}-panel`.
- `ZimmPdpDrawer`: generates `idPrefix` via React's `useId()` (unique even with the boutique
  `ZimmDrawer` also mounted on the same page); its panel now has `id={idPrefix}-panel`,
  `aria-labelledby` pointing at the *currently active* tab's id (updates on every switch), and
  `tabIndex={0}` — the last one is its own separate APG recommendation (a tabpanel needs to be
  in the Tab sequence when its content isn't itself reliably focusable), so `Tab` from the
  active tab now lands in the panel content before reaching the close icon.
- Updated `ZimmTabs`'s own story/test call sites for the two new required props; added 4 new
  Vitest tests (Home, End, tablist `aria-label`, per-tab `id`/`aria-controls`); added
  panel/tab-association assertions (`aria-controls` ↔ panel `id`, panel `aria-labelledby` ↔
  active tab `id`, before and after a tab switch) to `ZimmPdpDrawer`'s existing Storybook
  `play` functions rather than a new test file, matching that component's existing
  Storybook-only coverage precedent.

**Verified**: `tsc` clean, full `npx vitest run` 437/437 (10/10 in `zimmTabs`, up from 6),
ESLint clean, `audit:tokens` clean (same 4 pre-existing unrelated violations). Storybook-checked

## Fixed CI's "Storybook interaction & a11y tests" red (2026-08-31)

PR #67 (now out of draft, per the above) had this check failing. Reproduced locally with the
exact CI command (`npm run build-storybook` → `http-server storybook-static` → `test-storybook
--ci`), not just Storybook screenshots — this is `@storybook/test-runner`, a real Playwright +
axe run of every story's `play` function, distinct from the visual-only checks used earlier in
this session. Went from 5 failing suites/7 failing tests down to 0/0, confirmed stable across
two consecutive full runs.

**Two real, root-caused bugs (not test artifacts):**
- `ZimmTabs`'s own isolated story (`Elements/ZimmTabs`) set `aria-controls` pointing at a panel
  id with no matching element in that story — `ZimmTabs` owns no panel content by design (a real
  caller like `ZimmPdpDrawer` always renders one), so the isolated story needed the same
  pairing. Added a placeholder panel element with the matching id/role/`aria-labelledby`.
- `ZimmModal`'s `aria-labelledby`/`aria-describedby` were never reaching the actual dialog DOM
  node. Root-caused by reading `@chakra-ui/modal`'s own source: `ModalContent`'s internal
  `getDialogProps` unconditionally recomputes both from its own `ModalHeader`/`ModalBody`-mount
  tracking *after* spreading whatever props we pass, always overwriting them to `undefined`
  since ZimmModal's children never use Chakra's `ModalHeader`/`ModalBody`. A first fix attempt
  (plain `useRef` + `useEffect`) looked right but didn't work either — Chakra's Portal does its
  own two-pass mount, so that effect fired and read the ref before the real DOM node existed,
  and never re-fired once it did (none of its deps changed on Portal's later commit). Fixed with
  a `useState`-backed callback ref instead, which reacts to the actual node appearing.

**The rest were animation-timing gaps, not test-runner flakes** — real behavioural changes from
the earlier Chakra-Modal/Drawer rebuild (animated primitives replacing instant hand-rolled
ones) that several existing `play` functions never accounted for:
- `ZimmDrawer`'s `CloseButtonClosesTheDrawer` and Footer's `SubscribeSubmit`/Escape-dismiss all
  asserted a dialog's removal the instant after the closing action — Chakra's exit transition
  keeps the node mounted (mid-slide/mid-fade) for a beat first. Switched to
  `waitForElementToBeRemoved`.
- `ZimmModal`'s and `ZimmSubscribeModal`'s own stories asserted post-open state (and, via the
  a11y check that runs right after `play` returns, sampled colour contrast) without waiting for
  the fade-in to finish, so axe sometimes measured genuinely-passing tokens mid-blend as a false
  `color-contrast` violation — confirmed via DOM inspection that the underlying colours were
  correct once the transition settled. Added an explicit `waitFor(() => opacity === '1')` before
  each of those assertions.
- Footer's `SubscribeModalOpen` scroll-lock assertion checked `document.body.style.overflow`,
  which was the *old hand-rolled* ZimmModal's mechanism. The rebuilt (Chakra-based) ZimmModal
  locks scroll via `react-remove-scroll` (confirmed by reading its source), which uses a
  `data-scroll-locked` attribute instead — this assertion was checking a mechanism no longer in
  use, not a timing race. Updated to check the real attribute.

---
name: project-figma-metrics-rule
description: Figma TEXT nodes report a cap-height box and aren't comparable to CSS line boxes; frames and instances report real boxes and ARE comparable — check node type before calling a delta an artifact
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: f5f727b4-7546-4aa6-9d86-ef229e247d3f
  modified: 2026-08-22T14:05:00.000Z
---

**The discriminator is node type, not a fudge factor.** An earlier version of this memory said
simply "Figma reports the glyph box, CSS reports the line box." That's only true of **text nodes**,
and the missing half is what makes the rule usable:

- **Text nodes** report a **cap-height box** (`text-box-trim: trim-both`, `text-box-edge:
  cap_alphabetic`). **Not comparable** to a CSS line box. Measured artifacts: "KEEP IN TOUCH" 8 vs
  18, body copy 26 vs 36, `errorText` 9 vs 18.
- **Frames and instances** report a **real box**. **Directly comparable** — so a delta here is a
  genuine defect. The `Textfield` *instance* at 44/59 against our 45/68 was a real gap, and the
  naive "it's just cap height" rule would have wrongly dismissed it.

**Supporting heuristic:** a *uniform* residual across siblings is measurement; a *varying* one is a
defect. Three contact items all sitting at +7 after every real cause was removed = the heading's
cap box.

**Transfer the rule, not the numbers.** In shipped `zimmNavItem.ts`, deriving from `lineHeight` +
4.5px padding produced 24/24/24/24/38 = 134 — exactly Figma's `Links` frame.

**There are TWO Figma files and comparisons must be like-for-like from one:**
`wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm` (design system) and `QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs` (composed page states).
Comparing an initial state from the design-system symbol against an error state from the page file
produced two wrong conclusions in a row — first "the slot is 59px in both states" (actually
`Subscribed=False` 320×44 vs `Subscribed=True` 308×59, with a compensating gap change 40→24: the
design **repositions**, it doesn't reserve), then a "reserve the slot" fix that suppressed intended
growth when the 68px padded box was already design-correct.

**Frames are not breakpoints.** Frames exist at 402/1023/1440; breakpoint tokens are 768/860/1024.
The unframed **768–1022 band was genuinely broken** (18px horizontal scroll, 7 wrapped labels) and
covers three iPad models in portrait. `flexWrap: nowrap` prevents *breaking*, not *shrinking* — the
row refused to break so the words broke instead.

**No automated gate in this stack catches a layout defect.** `width: 'xl'` resolving through
`theme.sizes` (36rem) blew contact icons to 576px and destroyed the footer on every page while
passing tsc, eslint, vitest, local *and* remote CodeRabbit, and Storybook a11y. Only rendering
beside Figma found it.

**Method notes:** measure `y` relative to the component root (Figma reports frame-relative
coordinates); use `domcontentloaded`, never `networkidle`, on a dev server; dismiss the consent
banner first; `Range.getClientRects()` gives per-line widths to *prove* a wrap point;
`document.fonts.check()` returns `true` for unavailable families and is useless — compare widths
instead; and **mutation-test layout fixes at mobile**, since two fixes read as Δ0 at 1440 only
because a taller sibling column masked them.

**How to apply:** before calling any Figma-vs-code delta an artifact, check the node type. Text →
likely artifact, verify uniformity. Frame or instance → treat as real. See
[[feedback-prove-dont-assert]] and [[project-chakra-scale-registration]].
